The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.

Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.

Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches on offense to be worth considering in fantasy against Denver's stout defense in Week 2. He had one target and one carry in Jacksonville's season opener, which he turned into 11 scrimmage yards across four snaps on offense while playing primarily on defense. Hunter played both wide receiver and cornerback at Colorado before being drafted second overall by the Jaguars in 2025. With WRs Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers ahead of him, the versatile Hunter is currently more useful to the Jaguars on defense, much to the chagrin of his fantasy managers.

player.seasonOutlook: Full-time focus on defense should unlock rewarding production from a unique talent. Not only can Hunter mirror receivers, he frequently turns his head to track the ball, leading to big plays in coverage.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.

De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.

C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones is unlikely to post gaudy passing numbers in the Colts' run-first offense, and he doesn't appear interested in using his legs as much after tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of last season. His fantasy appeal is limited to multi-QB or superflex formats, and Jones is a low-end option even in those leagues for a Week 2 matchup against a Chiefs defense that held Bo Nix to 131 passing yards in Week 1. Jones had just 166 passing yards with a 1:1 TD:INT and one carry for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Ravens.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones re-signed with the Colts during the offseason and will return as the team's starter. The 2019 No. 6 draft pick made a big leap in 2025 -- his first season with Indianapolis -- finishing no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. Despite the strong play, Jones was inconsistent as a fantasy option, averaging 18.8 fantasy points during 12 full games and posting three top-five weeks but no additional finishes better than ninth. Jones was effective through the air and scored five rushing TDs, but he didn't run the ball as much as in years past and might do even less of that in 2026 after tearing an Achilles in Week 14. He's likely to be ready for Week 1, but effectiveness is a concern, so he's best viewed as a midrange QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.

Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.

Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. Despite leading Baltimore's receivers with 53 offensive snaps, he logged just one target and did not record a reception. With Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane out with a fractured wrist suffered in the opener, Bateman's opportunities to contribute could increase. Regardless of who's active, he'll aim to bounce back against New Orleans' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (37.2) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected. The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2. They'll face the fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.1) to WRs. Jeudy brought in two of four targets for 26 yards in Cleveland's season-opening blowout loss, but he didn't see any looks in the second half. He tied rookie Denzel Boston for second in targets and third in receptions, while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the way with four catches and five targets. As long as the Browns' QB play remains shaky, there's no reason to consider Jeudy in any fantasy formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Schultz was second on the Texans in targets behind Nico Collins during the season opener, which matched Schultz's usage last season. After being thrown to eight times in Week 1 against a Bills defense that allowed the fewest yards in the NFL to TEs last season, Schultz is poised for a hefty Week 2 workload against a Bengals defense that surrendered the most yards to his position in 2025. Schultz's role and matchup make him a top-10 fantasy TE for Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.

Sam Darnold suffered a soft-tissue glute injury in Seattle's season-opening win and isn't likely to play in Week 2 against Arizona. As a result, Drew Lock is in line to guide the Seahawks' offense. Darnold isn't expected to miss significant time and could be back as soon as Week 3.
