Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Legette appears to be an afterthought in Carolina's offensive game plan, as he received just two targets despite the team scoring 37 points in the Week 1 loss. He's clearly behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (ankle) in the WR room, so it's unlikely Legette will see much volume going forward. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed just 8.6 yards per completion in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Legette is eyeing a Year 3 leap after a boom/bust start to his NFL career. The 2024 first-round pick flashed with 521 yards and four touchdowns on 55 touches as a rookie, but fell to 363 yards and three scores on 36 touches in 2025. Legette did post a pair of big games (24.2 points in Week 7 and 18.3 points in Week 11), but was otherwise held in check (3.6 PPG in the other 13 games). Legette has struggled with the ball in his hands (woeful 2.1 RAC in his career) and is behind Tetairoa McMillan and likely Jalen Coker on the Carolina WR depth chart. The 25-year-old will see some situational targets and carries, but he'll need a big Year 3 leap to find his way to fantasy relevance. He's no more than a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable role for Buffalo, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.

Colby Parkinson will aim to be more productive when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Parkinson led Los Angeles tight ends with 47 offensive snaps in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he caught just one pass for six yards. The Rams had three other tight ends log at least 12 offensive snaps in the contest, so the week-to-week individual production among that group could vary widely throughout the season. The Giants held Dallas' starting tight end, Jake Ferguson, to just two catches for six yards in Week 1, so Los Angeles' tight-end corps could have trouble as a whole.

player.seasonOutlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few rounds in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cole Kmet will aim to stay involved as the Bears take on the Vikings in Week 2. Kmet brought in two of three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 1, and he was the only tight end to record a catch. While the veteran is set to be a secondary option behind Colston Loveland this season, the high-scoring ability of Chicago could allow plenty of targets for the pair. They'll face a Minnesota defense that gave up five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.

Daniel Carlson will look to remain productive in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Carlson converted his first four kicks (two field goals and two extra points) before missing a 62-yard field-goal attempt on the last play of regulation. He's expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities moving forward but may struggle against the Ravens in Week 2, as they allowed just 5.0 kicking points in Week 1.

Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 showdown against the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for 18 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Falcons. Washington and Pat Freiermuth were co-starters at TE, but the latter tallied five catches for 46 yards and a TD. New England's defense is very stingy against the position, as they rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (3.3) to tight ends.

player.seasonOutlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) could start if active for the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed eight total touchdowns to the Bears in Week 1. Tagovailoa was unable to suit up last week after sustaining an oblique injury in practice, which is likely a factor in why Atlanta's offense struggled so much. He struggled in 2025, throwing for 2,660 yards and 20 touchdowns while turning it over 16 times in just 14 contests. The Falcons' offense is in for a very favorable matchup, however, as Carolina gave up 334 total yards and five touchdowns to Caleb Williams last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta during the offseason after spending his first six seasons in Miami. The 2020 first-round pick showed signs of life a few years ago, which included a 4,624-yard, 29-TD season in 2023, but his production and efficiency have declined since. The final straw was a rough 2025 in which he threw 15 INTs (second most in the league) in just 14 games and was benched. Tagovailoa is a nonfactor with his legs (fewer than 75 yards in four straight seasons, with zero TDs during the span) and has, in turn, never finished better than 10th in fantasy points per game (he was 33rd in 2025). Even if Tagovailoa starts in Week 1, he's unlikely to be anything more than a fringe QB2 in fantasy and figures to eventually lose work to Michael Penix Jr. (recovering from a torn ACL). Tagovailoa is way off the fantasy radar.

Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

Singleton was selected by the Titans in the fifth round of April's draft. He is a big, versatile back with terrific speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. While working in a committee with fellow rookie Kaytron Allen at Penn State the past four years, Singleton was effective after contact (3.46 YAC is sixth best in this RB rookie class) but struggled with elusiveness (8.0 forced missed tackle rate is worst). He was solid as receiver (102-987-9) and returner (class-high 1,138 kick return yards) during his 53-game tenure. Singleton will open his career behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, but would make for an interesting waiver add in the event of a Pollard injury.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jack Bech was the only Raiders wide receiver to make much of a difference in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching three of four targets for 23 yards and a touchdown. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker, produced very similar numbers in terms of receptions and receiving yards. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Bech will look to continue building chemistry with Cousins in Week 2 against a Chargers secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bech is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 36% of Las Vegas' offensive snaps and cleared three targets in a game only twice. He failed to find the end zone while predominantly working as a short-range target. Bech will now compete with the likes of Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in a new-look offense led by coach Klint Kubiak and, at some point, No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is likely headed for a larger role in his second season and is worth a late-round flier.

A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahan Dotson is in for a great Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers, whose defense just allowed 12.4 yards per completion last week. Dotson played 38 offensive snaps during Atlanta's Week 1 loss, out-snapping Olamide Zaccheaus and rookie Zachariah Branch, who each logged 18 snaps. Additionally, he trailed only Bijan Robinson and Drake London in targets, despite only receiving three. Regardless, Dotson should be in for a phenomenal Week 2 matchup after Carolina's defense gave up 59 points and eight total touchdowns in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of the Washington backfield (Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt). If Allen impresses during the offseason, he could sneak onto the fantasy radar.

The seeds are here for the Cardinals to have a respectable pass defense -- Budda Baker, Josh Sweat and Will Johnson all return -- but a lot would need to go right for Nick Rallis' defense to become a fantasy force. As is, the Cardinals have one of the league's toughest D/ST schedules, largely due to their playing in last year's winningest division -- their three division rivals combined to go 38-13. But hey, they do have what could be a great fantasy-playoff schedule (NYJ, @NO, LV, from Weeks 15-17), if they show us anything early.

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ted Hurst will look to build on his solid NFL debut in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Hurst played 75 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps and caught all three of his targets for 36 yards, taking advantage of increased opportunities with Jalen McMillan (knee) sidelined. Hurst could continue being a valuable asset to Tampa Bay's offense if McMillan continues to miss time, which he very well could in Week 2. The matchup against the Browns is also great, with that defense allowing a whopping 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie-season fantasy production with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan in the fold.

outlooksByWeek.2: Troy Franklin had a small role in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, failing to catch his only target and gaining five rushing yards on one jet sweep. By contrast, Pat Bryant led the team with six targets and seems to be emerging as Bo Nix's most comfortable security blanket and the No. 3 receiver behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. Better days will be ahead for the Denver passing game, but Franklin has some work to do to earn meaningful production. He'll face a Jaguars defense in Week 2 that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Midway through the 2025 season, Franklin appeared well on his way to a Year 2 breakout. The 2024 fourth-round pick entered Denver's Week 12 bye with five touchdowns and a team-high 81 targets (22% share). He was demoted during the week off, however, and ended up with just 24 total targets (a 9% share) over his final seven games, including the playoffs. In total, Franklin finished a respectable 41st among receivers in fantasy PPG, but the 23-year-old's demotion, coupled with Denver's offseason acquisition of Jaylen Waddle, means he's nowhere close to the fantasy radar. Franklin will battle Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. Ignore him on draft day.

Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliable fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Fitzgerald is in for a favorable Week 2 matchup when the Panthers face the Falcons, who gave up 8.0 kicking points in a Week 1 loss. Fitzgerald made five of his six kicks last week, drilling his only field-goal attempt while going four-for-five on point-after tries. He's expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 2, as he averaged 11.0 kicking points per game in two games against Atlanta in 2025.

Tyquan Thornton saw only one target in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, failing to bring in a deep ball from Patrick Mahomes, and that sums up his role in the passing game. The former Patriot will hit for big plays on occasion, as 11 of his 19 receptions in 2025 went for 20 yards or more, but he won't see enough volume to be a reliable contributor unless injuries open up more volume for him. Thornton gets a more exploitable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last year.

Sione Vaki is poised to serve as Detroit's supplementary running back once again in Week 2 at Buffalo. While the Lions were planning to use a committee approach at RB2 this season, Vaki was the only other player at the position who saw the field behind star Jahmyr Gibbs. The third-year ball carrier recorded two rushes for seven yards and brought in his sole target for 11 yards. This makes it likely he'll be the main option behind Gibbs at least in the short term. Vaki will face a Bills defense that allowed 33.9 PPR fantasy points to RBs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with rookie Emmett Johnson for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Patriots in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. He caught three of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory versus Atlanta. Wilson tied for second on the team in targets and was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Despite the solid start, it's best he remains on benches or waiver wires until he can prove to be a consistent fantasy contributor.

Raheim Sanders and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. After Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out in the first half, Sanders filled in as the No. 2 RB behind Quinshon Judkins. He notched one carry for one yard and caught all three targets for 25 yards while playing 16 snaps on offense. With Cleveland expected to play from behind often, Sanders could have a fairly sizable role in the passing game, no matter who the quarterback is. Tampa Bay allowed eight catches on nine targets for 52 yards to RBs in their Week 1 loss.

Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 2 matchup against Seattle as the NFL's co-leader in field-goal makes. Ryland converted four of five FG attempts in a Week 1 win against the Chargers, matching his 2025 season-high mark for field goals in a game. However, the veteran kicker had just 25 FG makes last year, so it may not be wise to expect such volume on a weekly basis. The Seahawks don't figure to provide Ryland with as many scoring opportunities, as they led the NFL with just 17.2 PPG allowed during the regular season last year.

Joey Slye is unlikely to get many kicking opportunities in Week 2, when Tennessee's underwhelming offense faces the ferocious Eagles defense. The Titans generated just 195 yards of total offense in their 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, and Tennessee was a bottom-three team in both yards and points per game last season, while Philadelphia gave up the fifth-fewest points in 2025. Slye isn't known for his accuracy, either, so he isn't worth using in fantasy.

player.seasonOutlook: Tolbert signed with Miami after spending his first four NFL seasons in Dallas. The 2022 third-round pick has a path to a substantial offensive role, with Malik Washington and rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas as his top competition for snaps and targets. We have seen Tolbert as a near-full-time player in a much better offense and he wasn't much of a fantasy option. That came in 2024 when he played 76% of the Cowboys' offensive snaps. He found the end zone seven times, but was held to 610 yards and finished 54th among receivers in fantasy PPG. Tolbert played a reduced role last season and his 203 yards were the fewest since his rookie season. The 27-year-old has very limited upside and isn't worth much late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.

player.seasonOutlook: The rebuilding Dolphins are woefully lacking in talent on both sides of the football, and they're coming off a season in which they tied for 21st in fantasy points from the D/ST. An opening-week matchup against the Raiders could make them a viable streaming choice -- though that's directed more at you 12-, 14-team and Knockout managers ? but there's little else to like here, especially with one of the toughest overall schedules in the league ahead.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.

Tonges enters his fourth NFL season with no standalone value, but as a potential fringe TE1 should George Kittle miss any time. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson. Kittle (Achilles) is expected to be ready for Week 1, but if he's ruled out, Tonges will be a viable replacement.

Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart. The 23-year-old's primary value is as a dynasty stash.

McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

Beck was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of April's draft. Beck is a big, experienced quarterback who started for two seasons at Georgia prior to leading Miami to the national championship game last season. Beck paced this rookie QB class in completion percentage last season (72.4%) and for his career (69.5%), while also leading this group with an 80.9 QBR and 8.4 YPA during his 55-game collegiate career. He's unlikely to offer much with his legs in the pros, however, and will begin his career behind Jacoby Brissett and likely Gardner Minshew. Beck has no short-term fantasy value, though he could very well make some starts during his rookie season. Monitor him in superflex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Shipley managed just three touches for the Eagles in Week 1.  Meanwhile, fellow backup Tank Bigsby had just one carry for three yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Bills in the fourth round of April's draft. Bell is an undersized, but versatile, receiver who finished 2025 second in the nation (first in this WR rookie class) in receiving yards (1,278) and, while he had a class-high 25 drops across 52 collegiate games, he was better in this area last season (five drops on 146 targets). Bell showed well at the combine, running a solid 4.40 40-yard dash and posting terrific marks in the vertical and broad jump. With DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir locked in atop Buffalo's WR depth chart, Bell will compete with Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer for work. He's only worth drafting in dynasty formats.

A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andrei Iosivas and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. He hauled in two of three targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's season opener, tying Ja'Marr Chase in receptions despite Iosivas garnering 21 fewer snaps on offense. However, his role is limited with Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, and Mike Gesicki all healthy. Iosivas will remain locked in as the No. 3 WR versus Houston's 25th-ranked defense in yards allowed to receivers.

Kyle Williams' snaps could increase for the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Despite not drawing a target to open the season, Williams will likely ascend the depth chart following A.J. Brown's ankle injury that will sideline him for at least a month. Williams has shown big-play potential, so he may not require heavy volume to contribute, but until New England reveals its new receiving rotation, Williams can only be considered in the deepest of formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams showed some flashes as a rookie, but he has a tough path to a Year 2 breakout. The 2025 third-round pick didn't see the field much (31% snap share), but he scored three touchdowns on 21 targets, all of which came from Week 10 on. He was utilized as a situational deep threat (17.6 aDOT), which led to a low catch rate (48%) but plenty of big plays (20.9 YPR). That role may not change much in 2026, as Williams will now compete with newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, as well as incumbents DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for targets in a good New England offense led by Drake Maye. Unfortunately, he doesn't have a path to fantasy consistency and is best stashed only in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Randall was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. More specifically, he was handpicked by owner Steve Bisciotti. Randall is the biggest back in this rookie class and he possesses terrific speed (4.50 40-yard dash, 113 speed score), a combination that makes him an interesting developmental flier. A converted wide receiver, Randall had a grand total of four carries during his first three seasons at Clemson prior to posting a 168-814-10 rushing line in 2025. His experience as a receiver suggests he has big upside in that area, as well (he totaled an 84-787-5 receiving line with the Tigers). He has some 2026 insurance appeal, but he'll primarily learn the ropes behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill in 2026, with eyes on lead-back duties upon Henry's departure. Randall will begin the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hollywood Brown did not record a target in Week 1 for the Eagles. Meanwhile, rookie Makai Lemon was the No. 3 wideout behind DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, which included four targets in his NFL premiere. Brown looks like an afterthought heading into Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans allowed 215 yards passing and zero touchdowns through the air in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown signed with the Eagles and he's likely to slot in either third or fourth on the team's depth chart behind DeVonta Smith, first-round rookie Makai Lemon and perhaps Dontayvion Wicks. Once a featured target in Baltimore and Arizona, Brown was more of a situational player during his two seasons in Kansas City. He barely saw the field in 2024 due to injury before handling a career-low 14.2% target share in 16 games in 2025. Brown cleared 10 fantasy points three times, but all came prior to Week 7. With Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley also heavily in the mix for targets in Philly, Brown will have to beat out Lemon and Wicks for a starting gig in order to have any chance at flex value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Riley Patterson's floor remains low in a limited Dolphins offense entering Week 2 against the 49ers. While he had three field goal opportunities to open the year (making two), he converted only one extra point. Field goals likely aren't going to cut it with the Dolphins defense allowing points early and often, keeping Patterson off fantasy rosters.

Andre Szmyt and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. He finished Cleveland's 34-10 loss a perfect two-for-two on kicks, making a 26-yard field goal and connecting on his lone PAT. Tampa Bay gave up 33 points last week, but that was to an elite Bengals offense that isn't even in the same realm as the Browns. Szmyt should be left on waiver wires as long as Cleveland continues to struggle to create scoring opportunities.

player.seasonOutlook: Stowers was selected by the Eagles in the second round of April's draft. Stowers is a converted quarterback who improved his production each of the last three seasons, peaking with a 62-769-4 receiving line in 2025. He aligned in the slot on 72% of his collegiate routes (highest among this rookie tight end class) and his career 2.38 YPRR is easily tops in this TE class. He's not much of a blocker, but he sports good speed and athleticism (he posted the best vertical and broad jumps among TEs at the combine). Stowers will have minimal fantasy value while working behind Dallas Goedert as a rookie, but he has long-term TE1 upside and will be a popular breakout candidate in 2027.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mason Taylor will push for more involvement when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Taylor logged a decent 68% snap share to open the year despite Kenyon Sadiq being available but turned three targets into two catches for minus-two yards. Week 2 figures to be a more pass-heavy game script, and the Packers allowed six catches and a touchdown to the position in Week 1, but Taylor likely needs to prove he's part of the game plan before managers take notice and consider him a viable option.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor will play a role in the New York offense, but he won't see nearly enough targets to allow any sort of fantasy relevance.

Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the fantasy radar.

After failing to lock down a starting gig with the Bears, Steelers and Jets, Fields was traded to the Chiefs and will move forward as Patrick Mahomes' backup. That's obviously unlikely to lead to much playing time, barring a Mahomes injury. Should Fields start, he'll find his way into the QB1 discussion because of his elite rushing ability (45.1 rush rushing yards per game last season and four-plus rushing TDs in four straight seasons). In seven full games last season, Fields averaged 19.2 fantasy points, including 25 points in three of those games. He averaged 18.9 points with Pittsburgh in 2024 and 19.3 during his final two seasons in Chicago. Roster Fields in only deep superflex leagues.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Flacco re-signed with the Bengals and will back up Joe Burrow this season. The veteran quarterback made six starts for Cincinnati last season and showed well, totaling 14 touchdowns and four interceptions while averaging 19.9 fantasy PPG. The 41-year-old can still sling it, but he's a nonfactor with his legs and hasn't finished a season better than 20th in fantasy points since 2014. If Burrow is sidelined, Flacco will do enough through the air to land in the QB2 discussion, but that's his ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.

Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joshua Palmer's role within the Bills' offense is minimal at best entering a Week 2 matchup against the Lions. Palmer's snap share was 29% to open the season, and while his lone catch went for a big 34-yard gain, he drew just two targets. The passing game appears to flow through newly acquired DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, keeping Palmer on the fringe for production despite a terrific matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 yards in Week 1.

Chris Moore and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. On Monday, Baltimore reverted him to their practice squad, despite the receiver finishing second on the team with 53 yards on one catch. However, with Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane doubtful with a fractured wrist, Moore has a solid chance of being elevated to the active roster ahead of their tilt against New Orleans. He could be a name to monitor, with WR Devontez Walker (groin) also considered questionable to play.

Noah Gray collected plenty of snaps in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, playing 55% of the offensive snaps to Travis Kelce's 71%. However, the backup tight end logged only one target, which he turned into a five-yard reception. Gray is coming off his least productive season in 2025, posting a 21-178-0 line on 37 targets. He had produced a career-best 40-437-5 line on 49 targets the year before and is capable of occasional spike games with a healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. Gray gets a very favorable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts defense that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to TEs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

Sarratt was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round of April's draft. Surratt is a big, perimeter receiver who hauled in 31 touchdown receptions (most in this rookie WR class) in 40 collegiate games, which includes a FBS-high 15 in 2025. His efficiency was terrific across the board, including 10.7 yards per target, 2.69 YPRR and a 72% catch rate. Surratt is an intriguing prospect, but he may not see the field a ton as a rookie with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane also in the mix in Baltimore's low-volume pass attack. He's best as a dynasty stash.

Jones returns for his second go as Brock Purdy's backup in San Francisco after showing well in relief duties in eight starts last season. In those eight appearances, Jones completed 70% of his passes and threw 13 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 2021 first-round pick was a nonfactor with his legs (28-64-0), however, which limited him to an underwhelming 16.3 fantasy PPG. Should Purdy miss time in 2026, Jones will be no more than a fringe QB2. The 28-year-old shouldn't be considered on draft day.

Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of April's draft. Allar is one of the biggest quarterbacks in this rookie class and, while he has the arm to go with his frame, accuracy is a big concern. Allar was conservative during his time at Penn State (7.6 aDOT), but he still completed only 63% of his passes and averaged 7.4 yards per attempt. In 2025, he had the worst QBR in this rookie class prior to suffering a season-ending broken ankle. On the plus side, he could add value with his legs, as he posted a career 181-1,030-12 rushing line and his 8.3% scramble rate is second highest in this class. Allar will begin his career learning the ropes behind Aaron Rodgers and perhaps Mason Rudolph.

Heidenreich was selected by the Steelers in the seventh round of April's draft. Heidenreich is an intriguing prospect, as he's a tweener who could play running back or receiver in the pros. The Navy product never cleared 77 carries in a single season, but did post a 51-941-6 receiving line in 2025. For his career, he averaged 6.85 yards per carry and evaded one tackle for every 5.9 touches, both of which are best in this RB rookie class. He'll likely max out as a gadget player behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Lance is expected to play as the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Lance had a promising NFL debut, catching three of four targets for 42 yards. He was on the field for 62 of New Orleans' 90 offensive snaps, appearing to be the clear WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, and Tyler Shough looked Lance's way on a failed two-point conversion attempt in OT that would have won the game. While Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains sidelined, Lance should continue to be a valuable part of this Saints offense, especially with Shough attempting 56 passes in Week 1. Lance is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 7.8 yards per completion last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Lance was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of April's draft. Trey's little brother is the lone wide receiver in this rookie class who didn't play a single snap at the FBS level. However, he was productive as a perimeter receiver at North Dakota State, posting receiving lines of 75-1,053-17 and 51-1,079-8 over the last two seasons. He's a year or so older than most of his classmates, but he dominated at the combine with terrific showings in the 40-yard dash (4.34), vertical (41.5) and broad jump (133). He has the size and skillset to handle New Orleans' No. 3 gig behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele until first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson returns from injury. Lance's primary value is in dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kevin Coleman isn't a factor in the Dolphins' limited passing game ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. He collected just two targets in the team's opener, failing to record a catch. While Miami will be forced to throw from behind often in Week 2 and beyond, it doesn't appear as though Coleman will garner enough looks to be a fantasy consideration.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman Jr. was selected by the Dolphins in the fifth round of April's draft. Coleman is a small, slot receiver and punt returner who aligned inside on 83% of his 943 collegiate pass routes. Despite playing at three different FBS schools over the last three seasons, Coleman handled a solid 21% target share during the span and played well, catching 72% of his targets and dropping only four of 229 targets (1.7%). He posted a weak, 88 speed score at the combine, running a 4.49 40-yard dash at 179 pounds. Coleman will battle fellow rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, as well as a host of veterans for a role in a Miami offense likely to struggle to score points. He should only be drafted in dynasty.

Williams is primed for a larger role in his second NFL season. The 2025 third-round pick had a unique rookie campaign, handling more carries (11) than he did targets (10). Williams' gadget role allowed him only 90 snaps (12%) and he was utilized only near the line of scrimmage (1.4 aDOT). The Green Bay WR rotation no longer includes Romeo Doubs or Dontayvion Wicks, but Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and fellow second-year wideout Matthew Golden remain in the mix. Williams will need to beat out one (or perhaps two) of them and start to see more downfield targets in order to land on the fantasy radar. The 24-year-old is only worth late-round consideration in deeper formats, especially since he'll open the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonnu Smith will look to stay involved in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Smith was a solid option for Jordan Love in Week 1, converting two of his three targets for 50 yards. While the veteran remains an option behind Tucker Kraft, he should at least continue to be on the field and run routes. Smith will face a Jets defense that limited Titans tight ends to five catches for 35 yards in its opener.

Devontez Walker and the Ravens face the Saints and their 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs in Week 2. Walker, who has seven catches for 157 yards and four TDs across two seasons with Baltimore, sat out the Week 1 victory with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status in practice leading up to their clash with New Orleans, as the Ravens are pretty banged up at receiver. Zay Flowers (hamstring) is considered day-to-day while rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is doubtful, meaning Walker could have a chance to make some noise if he suits up in Week 2.

Jahdae Walker will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Walker made a mark in Chicago's season-opener win over the Panthers with his limited opportunities, reeling in his one catch for a one-yard touchdown. The second-year wide receiver could continue to see success this season, especially if the Bears continue to score at such a high rate. He'll face a Minnesota defense that allowed two touchdowns to Packers WRs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Benson's pro career is off to a slow start due primarily to a variety of injuries. The 2024 third-round pick was essentially splitting the Arizona backfield with James Conner last season, but he was never able to return to the field after suffering a knee injury in Week 4. He was effective prior to the injury, averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and was busy as a receiver (four-plus targets in three straight games). The 24-year-old will open the 2026 season on injured reserve and, even when healthy, he's no longer assured of a role with a new coaching staff and after the team added Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. Benson's best days are likely ahead of him, but his only shot at 2026 fantasy relevance is a new home or several injuries above him on the Arizona depth chart.

Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.

Barion Brown will likely have minimal offensive impact in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Brown played just seven offensive snaps in his NFL debut, suggesting he's clearly behind fellow rookie Bryce Lance (62 snaps) in the Saints' receiving corps. With Tyler Shough attempting 56 passes in the Week 1 loss, it's tough to imagine a better scenario for Brown to make an impact as well. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup against a Ravens defense that's given up just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tommy Tremble is expected to operate as Carolina's top tight end in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. The Notre Dame product led the Panthers' tight end corps in targets (five) and receptions (three) in the Week 1 loss, though he was outgained by Darren Waller (2-28-0). Tremble could very well operate as Carolina's No. 3 receiving option going forward, as Xavier Legette saw just two targets in Week 1. Additionally, Tremble is in for a great Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed 19.4 PPR fantasy points to tight ends last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Richardson enters his fourth NFL season as a backup to Daniel Jones. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passing style are the only reason to keep him stashed in deep dynasty leagues.
